The connect action opens a connection dialog initialized from the current session host, or from global FTP client, listing parser, passive mode and TLS defaults. It has General, Security, Advanced and Commands tabs. Required host/user/password are checked using trimmed text, and port accepts 0 through 65535; approved values retain their original whitespace. Blank user/password populate as `anonymous` and the global email preference. The implicit-SSL port is validated only when implicit SSL is selected. Advanced settings preserve implementation class choices, initial local/remote directory text, passive mode and raw post-login commands ([UI and browser details](ui-and-browser-details.md#connection-and-preference-dialogs)). On approval, `FTPSession.connect` chooses the configured FTP client and listing parser by class name, applies passive mode, timeout, buffer size and TLS settings, attaches event listeners, opens the control connection, authenticates, sends host-specific commands, enters the configured initial remote directory, and lists it ([ConnectAction.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/actions/ConnectAction.java#L43), [FTPSession.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/FTPSession.java#L617)). [PreferencesDlg](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/PreferencesDlg.java) provides General, Advanced, Proxy, Security, Transfer Modes, Regional Settings, UI, and Software Updates cards. Save validates the first seven panels in order, then calls all save methods (including Software Updates) and writes the global preference object. Restore Defaults repopulates every panel from a new `JFTPPreferences`. Cancel closes without invoking panel save methods, though “Check Now” in `SoftwareUpdatePrefsPanel` starts an updater immediately. [GeneralConnectionPrefsPanel](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/GeneralConnectionPrefsPanel.java) requires email and default local directory after trim, then stores the raw strings. [AdvancedConnectionPrefsPanel](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/AdvancedConnectionPrefsPanel.java) validates buffer size > 0 KB and timeout >= 0 minutes and converts those units when saving. [ProxyPrefsPanel](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/ProxyPrefsPanel.java) validates nonempty host and port 0–65535 only when enabled; blank/non-numeric port is caught, then saved as default 1080, and saving calls `JFTPUtil.updateProxySettings()`.

## Connection and trust flow

`FTPSession.connect` creates the FTP client/parser from the selected `RemoteHost`, applies passive mode, timeout, buffer size, SSL mode, and data-channel encryption settings, then calls [`JFTPSSLContext.getSSLContext`](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/ssl/JFTPSSLContext.java#L38) for SSL-enabled modes before registering control/data/FTP listeners and connecting. The caller uses the remote host name as the TLS host-name argument; SSL mode also controls implicit-port selection. This means TLS context construction and trust decisions occur before the FTP connection proceeds.

The connection boundary is the external `com.myjavaworld.ftp.FTPClient` API. `FTPSession.connect` reflectively constructs the selected client and `ListParser`, configures passive mode, timeout, buffer size, SSL mode and data-channel encryption, installs listeners, connects, logs in, issues configured commands, chooses the initial remote directory, and lists it ([FTPSession.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/FTPSession.java#L617)). The source uses FTP and FTP over SSL/TLS (explicit, implicit, or SSL-if-available modes); it contains no SFTP client or SFTP protocol path. The FTP API artifact's current availability and redistribution rights remain unverified; preserve its adapter boundary until those questions are resolved.

Save validates the first seven panels then invokes all eight save methods; Cancel does not save, though Software Updates “Check Now” starts an updater immediately even before Save/Cancel. Restore Defaults repopulates every panel from a new default bean. Introduction
------------

JFTP is a graphical FTP (File Transfer Protocol) client software for 
transferring files from one computer to another over TCP/IP networks such as 
Internet.

JFTP can connect to any system that has a valid Internet address and an FTP 
server program, allowing you to transfer files between a wide variety of 
systems, including Windows, Mac OS X, Linux, UNIX and IBM i(AS/400) systems.

JFTP integrates the most widely used and widely accepted security mechanism, 
SSL (Secured Sockets Layer), to securely transfer your business critical and 
sensitive data.

JFTP is written entirely in Java(tm), meaning, it can run on a wide variety of 
platforms such as Windows, Mac OS X, Linux, Solaris, HP-UX, OS/2, UNIX or any 
other platform with a compatible JVM (Java Virtual Machine). 

Features
--------

### "The Universal FTP Client"

A "true" Universal FTP Client. JFTP can be installed and run on a wide variety 
of platforms such as:

* Windows 
* Mac OS X
* Linux
* Solaris
